chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Mahbub from Ibn Ri'ab from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who killed someone accidentally in the Sacred Month. He said: The blood money is intensified upon him, and upon him is freeing a slave or fasting two consecutive months from the Sacred Months. I said: But something enters into this [i.e., the fasting period]. He said: And what is it? I said: The Day of Eid and the Days of Tashriq. He said: He fasts, for it is a right that has become obligatory upon him, and it does not contradict the first report, for the prohibition [of fasting] only applies to one who begins fasting [voluntarily]; but as for when two consecutive months are obligatory upon him according to what the report entails, then these days are obligatory for him to fast because he included himself in that [obligation].
ai.seo_question: Does accidental killing during the Sacred Month require fasting through the Days of Tashriq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the expiation (kaffarah) for accidental homicide during the Sacred Months involves paying blood money, freeing a slave, or fasting two consecutive months. He specifically addresses the potential conflict with the Days of Tashriq, ruling that the obligatory nature of the expiation overrides the prohibition on voluntary fasting, thereby requiring the individual to fast through these days to fulfill the divine command.
